evals.prompt: make a 12-second 9:16 instagram reel for Bean, a café in York. colours: coffee #2b1d14, cream #f3e6d3, accent #c8743a. line: “Coffee that takes its time”. we don't have a logo, make one from the name. no sound. and a version under 10 MB for WhatsApp
evals.expected_output: A film folder with the composition (index.html, fonts/, render.mjs, export.sh, check_film.py), a 1080×1920 master MP4 of about 12 s at 60 fps without an audio track, a version under 10 MB, a contact sheet and a summary with the chosen direction, the palette and typeface with the reason for them, the list of scenes and the assumptions made.
assertions: There is an MP4 at 1080×1920, 60 fps, 11–13 s long, without an audio stream (check_film.py without errors)
There is a version under 10,000,000 bytes
The reply or a working file contains the product's verb, three rejected obvious ideas with replacements and three clearly different directions, and the choice is justified
The video has a signature moment built from an element of this brand (e.g. a coffee bean), not just text sliding up from the bottom
The first frame has content (check_film.py does not warn about an almost uniform first frame)
Something unexpected happens every 5–8 s (a change of scale, colour, perspective or direction), visible on the contact sheet
The frames show the name “Bean” and the line “Coffee that takes its time” spelled correctly, each on screen for at least words × 0.3 s + 1 s
Text sits outside the top ~250 px and bottom ~400 px of the frame (areas covered by Instagram's interface)
The :root block has the colours #2b1d14, #f3e6d3 and #c8743a
The typeface comes from a local file, the reply says why it fits, and it isn't one of the defaults (Inter, Space Grotesk, Geist, Fraunces, Instrument Serif, Poppins, Montserrat, Urbanist)
check_film.py gives no warning about the template's demo palette or font, and the frames have no gradient text, glassmorphism or neon glow
There is no dot with a label above a heading and no — character on screen
The summary contains the chosen direction, the list of scenes, the assumptions made (e.g. the font) and a command to render again

evals.prompt: there's a finished video in evals/fixtures/film-demo. make it 25% slower and give me a version under 5 MB to send by email
evals.expected_output: A new render at speed 0.75 (the video gets a third longer, from 11.8 s to about 15.7 s), still at 60 fps, and a version under 5 MB. The reading of “25% slower” stated in the reply.
assertions: The pace was changed with the speed parameter (0.75) and a new render, not by stretching the finished video (setpts, minterpolate)
The new MP4 is 15.5–15.9 s long at 60 fps
The version to send is under 5,000,000 bytes
The reply states how “25% slower” was read (speed 0.75, the video a third longer)
Scenes and texts are unchanged apart from the pace

evals.prompt: make a 6-second logo intro, change to RewievLink, new name. colours like ours: warm white #f1f0ee, black #1c1b1a, orange #ff6a2b
evals.expected_output: The first message asks about the spelling (RewievLink or ReviewLink) and states in one sentence the reading: we show the new name, without the story of the change. The name lives in one parameter, so fixing the spelling is one render.
assertions: Before the first render the reply flags a possible typo (RewievLink instead of ReviewLink)
The video shows the new name, not an animation of the old name changing into the new one (caret, deleting letters, a “New name” label)
The name is set in one place (NAME)
The :root block has #f1f0ee, #1c1b1a and #ff6a2b, and check_film.py gives no warning about the template's demo palette
The reply contains a one-sentence reading of the brief and three directions to choose from or a recorded choice of direction
The video is 5.5–6.5 s long and has no audio track

evals.prompt: the video in evals/fixtures/film-demo looks generic, the colours and fonts are slop. it's for Kiln, a pottery studio in Leeds, we don't have a brand guide
evals.expected_output: The look changes, not the scenes: three rejected default looks with replacements, a palette as named values and a typeface with a reason (a local file with its licence), the demo palette and Urbanist replaced, check_film.py without look warnings, stills before and after.
assertions: The reply lists three default looks it rejects, each with a replacement
The new palette is written as named values with roles, and the :root block uses them

The typeface isn't one of the defaults (Inter, Space Grotesk, Geist, Fraunces, Instrument Serif, Poppins, Montserrat, Urbanist), comes from a local file with its licence, and the reply says why it fits
The look doesn't fall into the second wave (cream with a serif in italics and a terracotta accent, black with a single acid accent) without a stated reason
check_film.py --composition gives no warning about the template's demo palette or font
The scenes and their timing are unchanged
